quote: Erst vor Allem wichtig ein Beispiel zu finden, von dem sich die Unmöglichkeit der integrallosen Darstellung beweisen lässt
english: First of all it is important to find an example for which the impossibility of an integral-free representation can be proved; one must be able to do this formally, since the formula must be satisfied identically in w^(n), w^(n-1), ...
topic: Hilbert discusses solving Pfaffian-type differential equations without integrals (the 'diophantine' problem) by expressing the unknowns as functions of arbitrary functions and their derivatives, compares this to genus-0 algebraic relations, and considers transcendental relations between pairs of functions defined by partial differential or integral equations.

triage.modern_statement: Take an underdetermined ODE system, Monge/Pfaffian type: for example one equation F(x, y, z, y', y'', z') = 0 in two unknown functions y(x), z(x). Call it 'integral-free' (in modern terms, differentially flat, or explicitly integrable in Monge's sense) if its general solution can be written as functions of x, of an arbitrary function w(x), and of finitely many of w's derivatives w', ..., w^(n), with no quadratures. The note asks for one explicit system for which you can prove that no such representation exists. The proof would be formal: the substituted formula would have to hold identically in w, w', ..., w^(n).
triage.answered_by: Hilbert solved it himself. In 'Über den Begriff der Klasse von Differentialgleichungen' (Festschrift Heinrich Weber, March 1912; reprinted in Math. Annalen 73 (1912), pp. 95–108) he proved that the Monge equation z' = (y'')^2, now called the Hilbert–Cartan equation, has no integral-free general solution. W. Gross followed in Math. Ann. 73 with first-order systems whose solutions can be written without integrals. É. Cartan (1914) generalised the result. From the 1990s it was taken up as 'differential flatness' in control theory (Fliess, Lévine, Martin, Rouchon).

evidence.claim: Hilbert's paper 'Über den Begriff der Klasse von Differentialgleichungen' appeared in Math. Annalen vol. 73, pp. 95–108 (1912), reprinted from the Heinrich Weber Festschrift.
The Festschrift text defines classes of differential equations by reversible integral-free ('umkehrbar integrallos') transformations. This is the same notion as in the diary note.
W. Gross published 'Über Differentialgleichungssysteme erster Ordnung, deren Lösungen sich integrallos darstellen lassen' in Math. Ann. 73, right after Hilbert's paper.
A modern paper says Hilbert showed in 1912 that the Hilbert–Cartan equation (1.1) cannot be solved without integrals ('integral-free').
This paper discusses the 'Hilbert equation' and the more general z' = F(x, y, y', y'', z) studied by Cartan, and asks when such equations have integral-free solutions.
Control-theory literature traces flat systems back to Monge and to Hilbert's 1912 work on the general solution of Monge equations, continued by Cartan in 1914.
Necessary and sufficient conditions for differential flatness are still a research topic. The problem of Monge is named as the archetype of this integrability question.

triage.why: The note asks for a provable example of a Pfaffian/Monge system with no integral-free representation. Hilbert answered this himself in his 1912 paper with z' = (y'')^2. My dating of the note to before that paper rests on its content; I did not find a source that dates the diary page itself. The problem is not one of the 23 Hilbert problems or the 24th, but it is well known: the equation is now called the Hilbert–Cartan equation, studied by Cartan in 1914. Today it underlies differential flatness in nonlinear control. A general, checkable criterion for flatness is still being researched (e.g. Lévine), so the wider area is active even though this specific example question is settled.
